evidence: Ter. Eun. 5.8.39: vōs crēdere hoc mihi vehementer velim (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 96: vehementer ā tē dissentiō, I strongly disagree with you
terms.comment: With verbs of wishing, asking, approving and disliking: vehementer rogāre, displicēre (Cicero, Lewis & Short). Of action it is “violently, fiercely” (vehementer incūsāvit, Caesar), and with an adjective simply “very” (vehementer īrāta, Plautus).

terms.grammar: adverb: the ablative of opus with magnus, written as two words or one
evidence: Cic. Fam. 15.14.4: ego tibi Rōmam properandum magnō opere cēnseō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Chiefly with velle, petere, hortārī, cēnsēre: urging, advising or wishing hard. Literally “with great labour”. Lewis & Short: Plautus, Caesar and Livy write one word, Cicero’s best manuscripts two.

evidence: Cic. Att. 1.15.2: valdē aveō scīre quid agās
terms.comment: The everyday “very, very much” (see very); with a verb of wishing, “strongly, badly”.

phrases.latin: vōs crēdere hoc mihi vehementer velim
phrases.english: I would very much like you to believe me in this
